title: CLR/23/2017 of Suresh Chandra Saxena Vs Chandra Shekhar Joshi

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Civil Revision No. 23/2017
Suresh Chandra Saxena Ö. Revisionist

Versus
Chandra Shekhar Joshi .Ö Respondent
Mr. Sarvesh Agarwal, Advocate, for the revisionist.
Mr. Rajesh S. Nagarkoti and Vishal Singh Mahara, Advocates, for the
respondents.

Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
Having heard the rival contentions of the parties, I
feel that the Rent Control Act is not applicable in the
matter as the rent was more than rupees two thousand per
month. The revisionist herein has urged that he is an
indigent person inasmuch as a pauper and somehow by
doing some private job in a factory, he is pulling up his
family and meeting out day-to-day routine expenses. He
further apprised that he has been continuously paying
rent, but the landlord never issued any receipt to him.
The tenancy was only for 11 months. Thereafter it
was never renewed. So, it will be deemed to be day-to-day
tenancy and the termination has come into effect after the
notice was issued by the landlord and served on the
revisionist/tenant. Such notice has already been served on
the revisionist/tenant much before. Revisionist has lost
before the Court below. I also do not find any merit in this
revision. However, considering the plight of the revisionist,
he is granted time up 31st July 2017 to vacate the said
premises. Such time is granted provided the revisionist
furnishes an undertaking before the Trial Court that he
would vacate the demised premises by 31st July 2017
positively.

2
Revisionist shall also liable to pay the landlord @
Rs. 1000/- per month w.e.f. 3.9.2013. In case of any
default, the landlord shall be at liberty to get the decree
executed by due process of law.
With the directions/observations as above, the
revision stands disposed of finally.
